title: Queue fairness + KV batching lab digest — week of 2026-09-20
content:
Purpose
Quick digest of the lab we ran this week to test queue-fairness scheduling + KV-cache coalescing heuristics and how those interact with adaptive micro-batching. This is a working note — experiments still running in canary.

High-level summary
- Goal: reduce P95 latency tail for mixed-priority traffic without sacrificing throughput for high-throughput jobs.
- Approach: introduce a soft fairness token in the kernel scheduler that prefers older requests from low-priority queues when induced starvation is detected; pair with a KV-cache coalescer that biases prefill for long-context chat sessions.
- Outcome (so far): we saw ~18% improvement in P95 for low-priority short requests under mixed load, ~6% regression in P50 for aggressive batching workloads. Throughput (tokens/s) hold steady within ±3% on average.

Experiment setup
- Cluster: staging-rw-5 (8x A100-80GB), runtime build: serve-runtime@2026-09-22-fairqueue (branch: feature/fair-queue-heuristic)
- Traffic shape: 70/30 split high/low priority; mixed sequence lengths (mean=256 tokens, tail to 2048); synthetic replay + 10% live shadow production traffic.
- Config knobs tested (matrix):
  - fairness_alpha: {0.0, 0.25, 0.5}
  - coalescer_window_ms: {5, 20, 50}
  - micro_batch_max_tokens: {2048, 4096}
- Runs: each config run 30m steady-state after 10m warmup; repeated 3x for variance.

Key metrics (representative run)
- Baseline (no fairness, coalescer window=20ms, batch max=4096):
  - P50 latency (short reqs): 18ms
  - P95 latency (short reqs): 240ms
  - Throughput: 1.02M tokens/s
- Fairness_alpha=0.25 + coalescer_window=20ms + batch_max=4096:
  - P50: 19ms
  - P95: 198ms (–17.5%)
  - Throughput: 0.995M tokens/s (–2.5%)
- Fairness_alpha=0.5 + coalescer_window=5ms + batch_max=2048:
  - P50: 21ms (+16%)
  - P95: 176ms (–26.6%)
  - Throughput: 0.97M tokens/s (–4.9%)
Notes: numbers above aggregate short-only request latency; long-context sessions show smaller P95 improvements but better consistency in generation time (reduced jitter).

Observations / interpretation
- Fairness token helps reduce extreme tails for short low-priority requests by forcing occasional preemption of large micro-batches.
- Aggressive fairness_alpha (>0.5) starts to hurt batch efficiency (see P50 uptick) — expected tradeoff.
- Smaller coalescer_window (5ms) reduces unnecessary coalescing for low-latency paths but can starve the cache warm-up for long chat sessions; 20ms looks like a good middle ground in this workload mix.
- We observed a pathological case: when fairness_alpha=0.5 + coalescer_window=5ms + high incoming burst of long requests, a few kernels overloaded their queue leading to transient OOM on one host. Root cause likely race between coalescer prefill and allocator backpressure.

Concrete action items (owners + targets)
- INF-2381 (Jonas): add a soft backpressure signal from the allocator to the coalescer — if free KV pages < threshold, temporarily increase coalescer_window. Target: PR ready by 2026-09-30.
- INF-2392 (Ravi): add a telemetry metric for fairness_token_evictions and per-queue starvation_time to better debug long-tail behavior. Target: instrumentation merged by 2026-09-28.
- (Claire) Draft a canary plan to roll fair-queue with fairness_alpha=0.25 to a 10% slice for hosted API. Plan to run for 72h and compare P95 by customer tier. Canary PR: GH#1487. Deadline: 2026-10-01.
- (Mira) Re-run the pathological burst test with extra memory margin and log allocator traces; capture flamegraphs. Target: 2026-09-27.

Blockers / risks
- Allocator/coalescer interaction can cause transient OOMs in worst-case bursts — must be mitigated before larger canary.
- We lack fine-grained billing/test isolation for dedicated pools; can't fully simulate customer-perceived latency degradation with multi-tenant mixes in staging.
- Rolling fairness into Private deployments requires validation with KMS-bound models due to slightly different memory layouts; added to QA backlog.

Notes from sync (2026-09-24 retro style)
- Quick wins: enable fairness_alpha=0.25 in canary; add eviction metric (low lift) to detect issues early.
- Longer term: explore a hybrid scheduler that uses token aging + batch affinity scoring (score = age * priority / batch_size) — sketched idea on whiteboard, need a prototype.
- Ops suggestion (Ethan): expose a per-pool fairness override so platform teams can tune for specialized workloads (video transcription vs. chat). Good idea — add to product ask.

Outstanding questions
- What's the right default fairness_alpha for hosted API vs Dedicated? Should be config per pool.
- How much latency regression is acceptable for high-throughput customers for a given P95 improvement on low-priority traffic? Need product guardrails.

Next week plan (2026-09-27 -> 2026-10-03)
- Merge basic telemetry (INF-2392) and run live shadow for 48h.
- Jonas to implement allocator backpressure to coalescer (INF-2381).
- Start 10% canary rollout of fairness_alpha=0.25 on a single region for hosted API if no OOMs seen.
- Prototype hybrid scheduler sketch (spike) — goal: microbenchmark 2-week spike.
